podcast.title: Inspiration for Lollapalooza (1990)
podcast.body: While attending the 1990 Reading Festival with his band Jane's Addiction, Perry Farrell was deeply impressed by the atmosphere and had been contemplating a similar annual festival for new bands in North America. The sight of 30,000 Pixies fans singing along to "Debaser" solidified his conviction that his concept for what would become the Lollapalooza Festival would work.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 9

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Conception (1990)
podcast.body: Perry Farrell, inspired by the crowd's reaction to The Pixies at the Reading Festival in 1990, conceived Lollapalooza. He planned it as a traveling festival, partly to commemorate Jane's Addiction's farewell tour. "Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction was with some associates at the Reading Festival in the UK, and he was blown away by the crowd singing along to the Pixies as they played their song Debacer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Creator
podcast.body: Perry Farrell was the creator of the Lollapalooza Festival, a "traveling roadshow in circus" which held its second iteration in 1992, featuring a lineup described as arguably the best in its history. "This was the second year of Perry Farrell's traveling roadshow in circus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Farewell Tour and Lollapalooza (1991)
xref.body: Jane's Addiction initiated the first Lollapalooza tour, with Perry Farrell using it as a vehicle to commemorate the band's farewell tour. They retired for the first time in August 1991, after the tour's final show in Hawaii. "The fact that Perry needed some kind of hope to commemorate Jane's Addiction's Farewell tour also helped."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Founding Lollapalooza (1991)
xref.body: Perry Farrell, the singer for Jane's Addiction, conceived and established Lollapalooza in 1991, an "all-encompassing genre-bending traveling road show" that famously featured a mix of alternative rock and hardcore rap bands. This festival was groundbreaking in bridging racial and social barriers through music. "In 1991, Jane's edition singer Perry Farrell came up with the idea of an all-encompassing genre-bending traveling road show he called Lola Palusa."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Ever Tour (1991)
xref.body: The multi-act bill of the first Lollapalooza in 1991 was put together by singer Perry Farrell specifically to support what was intended to be Jane's Addiction's last ever tour. "the singer for Jane's edition put together a multi-act bill to support what would be the last ever tour for Jane's edition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Perry Farrell Sex Tape Leak (1998) – Multi-Million Dollar Lawsuit
xref.body: In 1998, a sex tape allegedly featuring Jane's Addiction singer and Lollapalooza founder Perry Farrell was leaked. The tape purportedly showed drug injections, sexual acts, and Satanic references. Farrell responded by filing a multi-million dollar lawsuit. "A sex tape was leaked purportedly showing drug injections, sexual acts, and references to Satan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Formation
xref.body: Eric Avery was the first to join Perry Farrell, with whom he spent time "goofing around." Eric then introduced Perry to his school buddies, guitarist Dave Navarro and drummer Stephen Perkins, both of whom were members of a metal band called Disaster. "Eric was the first guy to join up. He was one of James friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Communal Living in East Hollywood
xref.body: In the 1980s, Jane Bainter, Sergio, Perry Farrell, and approximately half a dozen other individuals shared a Victorian house on Wilton Street in East Hollywood. This communal living situation provided the backdrop for many of the personal experiences reflected in the song "Jane Says." "Jane, Sergio, Perry, and about half a dozen other people shared a Victorian house on Wilton Street in East Hollywood back in the 1980s."

xref.title: Influence on Scott Weiland's View of Heroin
xref.body: In the mid-1980s, Perry Farrell and Jane's Addiction "greatly influenced" Scott Weiland's perception of heroin, contributing to his romanticized view of its connection to rock and roll excess and creativity. "In the mid 80s, I had been greatly influenced by Perry Farrell and Jane's addiction."

xref.body: Perry Farrell, who attended the 1990 Reading Festival with Jane's Addiction, witnessed The Pixies' performance and the fervent crowd reaction to songs like "Debaser." This scene, with 30,000 fans singing along, was the decisive factor that convinced Farrell his idea for an annual North American festival (Lollapalooza) could succeed.

xref.title: Inspiration for Lollapalooza
xref.body: At the 1990 Reading Festival in England, a set by the Pixies saw a field full of kids "losing their minds," which directly inspired Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction to create the Lollapalooza Festival in the United States. "What he saw was a field full of kids losing their minds to a pixie set at the 1990 Reading Festival in England."

xref.title: Jane Bainter's Later Life and Estrangement
xref.body: By the end of the century, Jane Bainter had achieved sobriety, being clean for eight years, and successfully made her desired move to Spain. However, she eventually fell out with Perry Farrell and the band, resulting in her being snubbed and denied entry to their shows. Furthermore, she has received no financial compensation from anything related to the band or its music. "The good news is that by the end of the century, she had been clean for eight years and did end up going to Spain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jane Bainter: Muse and Namesake
xref.body: Jane Bainter was not only Perry Farrell's ex-housemate and a muse for his lyrics, but she is also the namesake for the band, "Jane's Addiction." She was described as having a posh, aristocratic air and being very intellectual, with her picture featured in the artwork of the band's indie debut album. "Many fans don't know that there really is a Jane who said a bunch of these things. Her name was Jane Bainter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Voicemail to Perry Farrell
xref.body: At some point before his death, Taylor Hawkins left a voicemail for his friend Perry Farrell, saying, "take care of each other, and I'll take care of myself. And I'll see you in São Paulo. I love, love, love you. Sleep well." These words are considered to be potentially his final communication. "He said, take care of each other, and I'll take care of myself. And I'll see you in São Paulo. I love, love, love you. Sleep well."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Limited Fanbase, Major Influence
xref.body: Despite not having a large fanbase at the time, The Pixies were highly regarded by influential figures. One such figure was Perry Farrell, founder of Jane's Addiction, who found them amazing and was inspired by their live performance at the Reading Festival. "But there were a few key people who thought they were amazing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza Conception
xref.body: Perry Farrell, inspired by the Pixies' performance at Reading on August 26, 1990, conceived Lollapalooza. The festival was initially designed as a farewell tour for Jane's Addiction, masquerading as a broader music festival to get off the ground. "Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction saw the reaction they got at Reading on August 26th, 1990. He thought to himself, why can't we have this kind of thing in America? And this is when we finally get into how the alt rock nation of the 90s got the North American festival scene kickstarted."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza Festival Conception
xref.body: Singer Perry Farrell conceived the idea for the Lollapalooza Festival in the summer of 1990 after witnessing an enthusiastic crowd at a Pixies set during the 1990 Reading Festival in England, prompting him to want to replicate such an event in the US. "Perry Farrell came up with the concept of the Lala Pulusa Festival in the summer of 1990."

xref.title: Lollapalooza Inspiration and Headliner Status
xref.body: Perry Farrell, the band's founder, was profoundly inspired by seeing The Pixies perform at the 1990 Reading Festival, leading him to conceptualize a similar festival for America. Jane's Addiction subsequently headlined the inaugural Lollapalooza tour, which ran from July 18 to August 28, 1991. "The first La La Paloza tour started on July 18, 1991 and ended on August 28. It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners."

xref.title: Other Creative Pursuits and Cocaine Psychosis (1990s)
xref.body: During his period of addiction and depression, John Frusciante focused on painting, attempting to write screenplays, and making demos on a four-track recorder. He also appeared with the band P, which included Johnny Depp and Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers, though nothing substantial came of it. He experienced severe cocaine psychosis from excessive crack and coke use, leading to days-long binges. During one such episode, he called Perry Farrell at 7 AM, asking, "how do you get the snakes out of your eyes?" He also described an elaborate outfit for "waging war against the ghosts" from his roof, covering every part of his body. "My outfit for going up on the roof to wage war against the ghosts. Goggles and my ski mask, with every part of my body covered. No holes, sweatpants tucked into my socks. You couldn't get into me on any level. It made sense at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Perry Farrell's Stage Presence
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins recounted witnessing Jane's Addiction's Perry Farrell performing with green dreadlocks and a woman's hat during their "seven nights up here in LA." Farrell's audacious and "crazy" stage persona deeply impressed Hawkins, who considered them "the best at that time." "Perry Farrell came out on stage with green dreadlocks. Woman's hat on and told the first guy in the front row to... The second he came out on stage, and I was like, these guys are crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Perry Farrell's Stephen Perkins Myth
xref.body: Perry Farrell was known for concocting an elaborate myth about Stephen Perkins, claiming the band's first drummer was a Tahitian canary smuggler who died of an overdose, and Stephen was allegedly his twin brother and a former boyfriend of actress Jodie Foster. The narrative explicitly states this myth is not to be believed. "He concocted this myth that the band's first drummer was actually a guy from Tahiti who made a living smuggling canaries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prisoner's Charity Work
xref.body: Wayne Kramer dedicated time to working with a prisoner's charity, collaborating with notable musicians such as Tom Morello, Billy Bragg, Perry Farrell, and Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains. "He also worked with a prisoner's charity alongside Tom Morello, Billy Bragg, Perry Farrell, and Jerry Cantrell of Ellison Chains."

xref.title: Views on Heroin Culture
xref.body: Weiland openly admitted his love and intrigue for heroin culture, referencing influences from William S. Burroughs, Charlie Parker, the aesthetic of The Rolling Stones, John Lennon's heroin period, and the mid-80s impact of Perry Farrell and Jane's Addiction. He associated heroin with romance, glamour, danger, and rock and roll excess, and was curious about its connection to creativity. "The truth is that I loved heroin culture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
